---
title: "Sjónabók pattern synthesis"
subtitle: "Growing new knitting patterns in the vein of Íslensk sjónabók"
toc: false
---

HiDEF Textiles is building a reproducible way to generate new two-colour knitting charts that look as if they belong in *Íslensk sjónabók*, the collection of old Icelandic embroidery patterns. The first target is a long banner, in the spirit of a *refill*: border bands along both edges, the book's motifs on a centre line, and new stitches that blend one motif into the next. It is 85 needles wide for the Passap E6000 and, in principle, endless.

This site explains the methods we have tried, in plain words, and shows what each one does on the same banner. In every chart you can switch between **Pattern only** (the two-colour knit) and **Copied vs new**, which colours what is taken straight from the book grey, invented stitches blue, and invented stitches that happen to recreate an exact 8×8 block from the book ochre.

```{=html}
<div class="banner-viewer" data-method="evolve"></div>

```

## The methods

| Method | In one line | How it looks |
|---|---|---|
| [Wave function collapse](methods/wfc.qmd) | Sudoku with stitches: every 3×3 patch must occur in the book | Sparse, broken up |
| [Stitch-by-stitch sampling](methods/sampling.qmd) | Look at the neighbours, copy what the book did | Dense, flows out of the motifs |
| [Image quilting](methods/quilting.qmd) | Patchwork of small pieces cut from the book | Dense, continues the motif texture |
| [Symmetric connector](methods/symmetric.qmd) | Invent half a bridge, mirror the rest | Ornamental bridges between motifs |
| [Cellular automaton](methods/cellular.qmd) | One simple rule computes each row from the last | Crisp geometric lattices, not book-like |

: {.method-table}

Two settings change every method: [how far apart the motifs are](banner/spacing.qmd), and [whether the motifs themselves are new](banner/evolve.qmd). [An endless banner](banner/endless.qmd) explains how any part of the banner can be regenerated exactly.

## Where this is going

The [roadmap](roadmap.qmd) lists the decisions still open before the C++ implementation. The [literature review](review/index.html) covers the research behind each method. Colouring (up to four colours, two per knitted row) is deliberately left until the patterns are right.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
